title: Tested one mechanic with 10 people. The feedback completely contradicts itself
author: Banana_Leclerc9
selftext:
Throw together a rough single-mechanic demo over the weekend just to see if the core loop held up. used something like Combos for a rough disposable draft, not trying to replace a real engine, just enough to get something playable and gather some messy feedback 

sent it to 10 people from a discord server. not friends, actually players who play the genre.

the responses split weirdly. four said it felt repetitive after 90 seconds. three wanted more. two didnt finish at all. And one guy said "cool but whats the goal."

So now i have raw data pulling in three directions and no clue what to prioritize. Do I scrap the idea entirely? tighten the pacing and retest? or add a second mechanic to see if it fixes the loop?

how do you weight conflicting playtest feedback when there is no clear majority?

comments.author: lbandy
comments.body:
You make each playtest answer one (or many) specific questions. What was the question you ASKED with that playtest, and what was the answer to that question from the 10 people? To see "if the core loop held up" is not a question, so the feedback you got is not directly actionable.

Advice: state the question, refine the build to help answer that question, and ask it directly when sharing with people. You only spent a weekend so far, and three players wanted more, so it's worth pushing forward to get clarity on why they wanted more (and why others didn't).

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
This is a combination of your test build not being robust enough, and your sample being poor.

"Ten randos on a discord server" does not make a good sample - you got *exactly* the expected feedback from a group like that.  Likewise, your build probably wasn't robust enough to be representative of gameplay, a "single mechanic demo" is pointless if that mechanic wasn't truly representative of your gameplay loop.  Was your "single mechanic" an entire roguelike dungeon run, or "this is my kick button for a fighting game?"  Totally different things.

comments.author: ReleasePossible2731
comments.body:
How exactly did you collect the feedback? Were you on a call with them or next to them when they played? Was there a form? What questions did you ask? 

I prefer being next to them when they are playing and just observe, this gives way more data than a form. And after we can talk. I’ve seen people say it’s great and works for them, but I SAW them skip stuff and be bored. I’d trust what i see.

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body: Just post a link here and all questions shall be answered.

comments.author: DrBimboo
comments.body:
What the fuck, why would you tell your AI to write with errors? 

If you let AI write your posts, at least let it write properly.

  
Now we get your thoughts through an AI filter, but still not properly written.

replies.author: DrBimboo
replies.body: Arent you also absolutely confused why the hell anyone would employ an AI to write badly for themselfes?

comments.author: Am_Biyori
comments.body: I'd find the results very informative. The 'what's the goal' sounds like a variation of 'repetitive' and it's believable the 'didn't finish' did so for the same reason. That's 70% saying the core mechanic isn't bad, but it needs a reason to be used.

comments.author: Calenart
comments.body:
Well, if you don't know what your game should be about, why other people should? I think you must rethink the definitions of your game project and what it should feel for the players.  
  
Also, every person has different experiences and ideas of what is fun for them, so... Be specific when asking questions to receive feedback, then you'll receive the answers you need. If you just go and "please send me feedback" people will tell anything that is coming in their minds at the moment for no particular reason.

comments.author: silly_bet_3454
comments.body:
That feedback doesn't seem contradictory at all. More content, less repetitive (meaning more variety and more mechanics maybe and more progression), and more hand holdy, these are all independent aspects.

Contradiction is when one person goes "the enemies are too easy" and another guy says "the enemies are too hard"

comments.author: Rude_Context_4844
comments.body: The "what's the goal" guy just saved you three months. Buy him a coffee
